title: Serial hardware adapter

parent.objective: Bring up a host-side bridge for the fictional SYNTH-SENSOR-1 so that every component is verified independently and no hardware behavior is claimed before it is observed.
parent.milestone: Adapter host rules verified; physical read attested

goal: Bind the Transport contract to a serial port through an injected opener, enforcing framing, timeout and close-on-error rules.
non_goals: Claim physical compatibility from fake-port tests.

allowed: Record the operator-run hardware-in-loop observation as a hardware evidence record.
prohibited: Edit codec, transport, device or telemetry modules.
Attest the hardware-in-loop check as the implementer.

inputs.name: Port contract
inputs.description: write(bytes) -> int, read(size, timeout_s) -> bytes returning what arrived within timeout_s, available() -> int reporting the currently buffered byte count without blocking or consuming it, close().

inputs.name: Host rules
inputs.description: Read one whole frame by declared length within the caller's timeout, handing each port read the time remaining; any failure on the wire — a frame left incomplete at the deadline, a short write, an oversized frame, a port call that raises — closes the port before it propagates; only a timeout that consumed nothing leaves it open; closed adapter refuses I/O. A zero-timeout receive polls at most as many bytes as available() reported before it touched the port, so an already-buffered frame is assembled whatever the port's chunking, while a byte that arrives only after that poll is never returned as received in time.

inputs.name: Hardware-in-loop procedure
inputs.description: SRC-HIL-PROCEDURE: operator connects a physical SYNTH-SENSOR-1 and runs one read through SensorDevice(SerialAdapter).

outputs.name: Adapter module
outputs.description: SerialAdapter implementing Transport over an injected Port.

outputs.name: Hardware evidence record
outputs.description: Bound record of the physical read: device identity, firmware, setup, expected and observed behavior.

assumptions: Fake-port tests establish host-side rules only; the physical rung is an operator observation.

acceptance_criteria.description: Every host-side rule holds against the fake port.
One read through the adapter against a physical SYNTH-SENSOR-1 returns a decodable reading, as observed and recorded by a non-implementer operator.

validation.description: Run the adapter tests with the fake port.
Operator performs one physical read per SRC-HIL-PROCEDURE and records a hardware evidence record.
evidence_required: Hardware evidence record digest bound in the attestation.
Device identity and firmware version as observed.
Observed reply frame and decoded reading.

architecture_boundaries: Serial port access exists only in adapter.py.
The Transport contract is not changed.

hardware_assumptions.assumption: The host serial driver delivers bytes in order and read(size, timeout_s) returns what has arrived within timeout_s, never blocking past it.
The host serial driver also reports, via available()/in_waiting, exactly how many bytes are currently buffered without blocking or consuming any of them.
A physical SYNTH-SENSOR-1 replies within the adapter timeout.
